report:
**Conclusion**
The health claim is well-supported by robust clinical evidence: daily subcutaneous abaloparatide significantly reduces the risk of new vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

**Evidence**
In the pivotal Phase 3 ACTIVE (Abaloparatide Comparator Trial In Vertebral Endpoints) randomized controlled trial, 18 months of daily abaloparatide reduced the risk of new morphometric vertebral fractures by 86% compared to placebo in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis (0.58% vs. 4.22%, *p* < 0.001) [https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640]. Abaloparatide also produced significant gains in bone mineral density (BMD) at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, and total hip [https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jbmr.2991].

Subsequent meta-analyses confirmed that abaloparatide consistently provides superior vertebral fracture risk reduction relative to placebo [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38307725/]. Furthermore, findings from the extension trial (ACTIVExtend) showed that initial treatment with abaloparatide provided sustained fracture risk reduction when followed by antiresorptive therapy [https://academic.oup.com/jbmr/article/34/12/2213/7380871]. Based on these clinical data, regulatory authorities (including the U.S. FDA) approved abaloparatide for treating postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture.

**Sources**
1. JAMA Clinical Trial Results: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640
2. Journal of Bone and Mineral Research (ACTIVE Study): https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jbmr.2991
3. Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38307725/
4. Journal of Bone and Mineral Research (ACTIVExtend Study): https://academic.oup.com/jbmr/article/34/12/2213/7380871
